page: The Microsoft Azure E2as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eav6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AES cryptography, and SHA extensions. No local storage or public IPv4 addresses are bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The E2as_v6 demonstrates strong single-core performance, scoring in the top 25% for both stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core evaluations. However, due to its low core count, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory performance is mixed; while the PassMark memory score and large-block write bandwidth are average, the read-only small-block memory bandwidth is poor, placing in the bottom 10%. Database operations and medium-model LLM text generation also score poorly, reflecting limitations in high-throughput data processing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E2as_v6 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio within a low-resource footprint, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is well-suited for light memory-intensive tasks, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and small-scale web serving. However, it is not recommended for heavy database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, or complex LLM inference due to its weak multi-core scaling and constrained memory read bandwidth.
